#### Intro: 

+--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Definition   | - Amount of energy spent on breathing                                                   |
|              | - Unit joules                                                                           |
|              | - = Force x displacement                                                                |
|              | - = Pressure work x volume work                                                         |
+--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Normal value | - \<2% total VO~2~ = 3mL/min                                                            |
+--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Efficiency   | - Only 10% (90% → heat)                                                                 |
+--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Components   | - Inspiration: primary active                                                           |
|              |   - Diaphragm, external intercostals etc                                                |
|              | - Expiration: secondary active at rest (use stored energy), primary active under stress |
|              |   - Abdominal wall, internal intercostals etc                                           |
+--------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Elastic (50%)

+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Surface tension     | - LaPlace’s law: pressure = 2 x surface tension / radius                   |
|                     |   - Fluid surfaces acquire least surface area due to surface tension       |
| (35%)               |   - Alveoli tend to collapse                                               |
|                     | - Surfactant:                                                              |
|                     |   - Produced by type 2 alveolar cells                                      |
|                     |   - Reduces surface tension at air-water interface                         |
|                     |   - Becomes more concentrated (= more effective) at low alveolar volume    |
|                     |   - →↓ alveolar collapse, ↑compliance, ↓ work of breathing, ↓ transudation |
|                     | - Factors increasing surface tension:                                      |
|                     |   - Alveolar oedema → surfactant dilution                                  |
|                     |   - Surfactant deficiency (e.g. prematurity, SP-B or SP-C deficiency)      |
+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Elastic lung tissue | - Elastic lung fibres e.g. elastin                                         |
|                     |   - e.g. fibrosis → ↓ elasticity → ↑WOB                                    |
| (15%)               |                                                                            |
+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Inelastic (50%):

+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Resistance to airflow | **Flow type:**                                                                 |
|                       |                                                                                |
| (major)               | - Large airways: turbulent flow – (P~1~-P~2~) ∝ (density x length) / radius^5^ |
|                       | - Small airways: laminar flow – R = (8 x length x viscosity) / (π x radius^4^) |
|                       | - Medium size: transitional flow                                               |
|                       |                                                                                |
|                       | **Variables: factors ↑resistance**                                             |
|                       |                                                                                |
|                       | - ↓Airway radius:\                                                             |
|                       |   \*Most important factor since raised to power of 4 or 5\*                    |
|                       |   - ↓Absolute lung size (e.g. neonate cf. adult)                               |
|                       |   - ↓Relative lung volume (e.g. diaphragm displacement in pregnancy)           |
|                       |   - Intraluminal obstruction (e.g. mucus)                                      |
|                       |   - Luminal obstruction (bronchoconstriction, swelling)                        |
|                       |   - Extraluminal obstruction (e.g. dynamic airways compression)                |
|                       | - ↑Density: e.g. reduced with heliox                                           |
|                       | - ↑Viscosity: e.g. ↑ with ↑temp                                                |
|                       | - ↑Length: not under control                                                   |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Inelastic lung tissue | - Deformation of inelastic tissue e.g. collagen                                |
|                       | - Also friction of lung vs pleura, diaphragm vs abdominal viscera              |
| (minor)               |                                                                                |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Inertia of air        | - Force = mass x acceleration                                                  |
|                       |                                                                                |
| (minimal)             |                                                                                |
+-----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

![](/content/exams/anzca/2001/B/2/prize-image003.jpg){fig-alt="Elastic, inelastic and total work of breathing against respiratory rate"}

                             **Neonate**   **Adult with asthma**
  -------------------------- ------------- -----------------------

  Airflow resistance         ↑             ↑↑↑
  Optimal respiratory rate   High          Low
